source.text: מִזְמ֖וֹר לְדָוִ֣ד לְהַזְכִּֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: A psalm of David. To bring to remembrance.

en.L: A psalm of David. To bring to remembrance.
en.B: A psalm of David. For remembrance.
en.R: A song of David. To call to mind.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: to bring to remembrance: to call to mind before God
decisions.reason: The verb (zakar, in the causative) means to cause to remember. It heads this psalm and Psalm 70. It may mean that the psalm calls the sufferer's need to God's mind, or that it was sung with the "memorial portion" of the grain offering ('azkarah, Leviticus 2:2), a word from the same root.

decisions.choice: A song; To call to mind
alternatives: A psalm; To bring to remembrance
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words, as in the other titles; the sense of the phrase is uncertain (m2).

source.text: יְֽהוָ֗ה אַל־בְּקֶצְפְּךָ֥ תוֹכִיחֵ֑נִי וּֽבַחֲמָתְךָ֥ תְיַסְּרֵֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: YHWH, do not in your anger rebuke me, and in your wrath discipline me.

en.L: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, do not in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger rebuke me, and [do not] in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wrath discipline me.
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} must rebuke me, let it not be in anger; if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} discipline me, let it not be in fury.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, do not be angry with me when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} correct me. Do not punish me while {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are furious.

decisions.choice: the same plea as Psalm 6:2
decisions.reason: The first line is nearly the same as 6:2. The psalmist does not ask to escape correction, which he knows he deserves (verses 4-5, 19), but that it not come in the full heat of anger.

decisions.choice: discipline: correct, as a father does
decisions.reason: The verb (yasar) is to train or correct, often as a father corrects a son (Proverbs 3:11-12).

source.text: כִּֽי־חִ֭צֶּיךָ נִ֣חֲתוּ בִ֑י וַתִּנְחַ֖ת עָלַ֣י יָדֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: For your arrows have sunk into me, and has come down upon me your hand.

en.L: For {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} arrows have sunk into me, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand has come down upon me.
en.B: Your arrows have driven deep into me; {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand weighs down on me.
en.R: It is as if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have shot me with arrows. Your hand is pressing down hard on me.

decisions.choice: your arrows, your hand: suffering sent by God
decisions.reason: God's arrows and his heavy hand are pictures of pain and illness that the psalmist receives from him (Job 6:4; Psalm 32:4).

decisions.choice: sunk, come down: one verb used twice
decisions.reason: The same verb (nachat, to come down) describes the arrows sinking in and the hand pressing down.

decisions.choice: It is as if you have shot me with arrows
alternatives: Your arrows have sunk into me
decisions.reason: Readable marks the arrows as a picture (m1).

source.text: אֵין־מְתֹ֣ם בִּ֭בְשָׂרִי מִפְּנֵ֣י זַעְמֶ֑ךָ אֵין־שָׁל֥וֹם בַּ֝עֲצָמַ֗י מִפְּנֵ֥י חַטָּאתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: There is no soundness in my flesh because of your indignation; there is no peace in my bones because of my sin.

en.L: There is no soundness in my flesh because of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} indignation; there is no wholeness in my bones because of my sin.
en.B: Nothing in my body is healthy, because of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} fury; nothing in my bones is whole, because of my sin.
en.R: My whole body is sick because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are angry with me. My bones ache because of the wrong I have done.

decisions.choice: illness, God's anger and sin linked
decisions.reason: The psalmist sees his illness as coming from his sin and God's anger. The Bible does not teach that all illness comes from a person's own sin (John 9:2-3; Job), but this sufferer knows his own guilt and says so.

decisions.choice: peace: health, wholeness
decisions.reason: Shalom here is the soundness of the body, in parallel with "soundness" in the first line.

source.text: כִּ֣י עֲ֭וֺנֹתַי עָבְר֣וּ רֹאשִׁ֑י כְּמַשָּׂ֥א כָ֝בֵ֗ד יִכְבְּד֥וּ מִמֶּֽנִּי׃

records.literal_gloss: For my iniquities have passed over my head; like a heavy burden they are too heavy for me.

en.L: For my iniquities have gone over my head; like a heavy burden they are too heavy for me.
en.B: My sins have closed over my head; like a heavy load, they weigh more than I can bear.
en.R: My sins are like deep water over my head. They are a load too heavy for me to carry.

decisions.choice: passed over my head: like floodwaters
decisions.reason: Waters that pass over the head are a picture of being overwhelmed (Psalm 69:3; 124:4-5); the second line adds the picture of a load.

decisions.choice: iniquities: wrongs and the guilt they bring
decisions.reason: The word ('avon) means both the wrong done and the guilt that follows it, which is why it can be a burden.

decisions.choice: like deep water over my head
decisions.reason: Readable names the picture (m1).

source.text: הִבְאִ֣ישׁוּ נָ֭מַקּוּ חַבּוּרֹתָ֑י מִ֝פְּנֵ֗י אִוַּלְתִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: My wounds stink, they fester, because of my folly.

en.L: My wounds stink, they fester, because of my folly.
en.B: My sores are foul and rotting, all because of my own foolishness.
en.R: My sores smell bad and are infected. It is because I have been foolish.

decisions.choice: folly: moral foolishness, sin
decisions.reason: The word ('ivvelet) in Proverbs is the foolishness of a person who ignores God's way (Proverbs 14:9); here it is another word for his sin.

decisions.choice: my wounds: sores of a real illness, or a picture
decisions.reason: The psalm may describe real sores and sickness, or use them as a picture of his state; it moves freely between body and feeling.

source.text: נַעֲוֵ֣יתִי שַׁחֹ֣תִי עַד־מְאֹ֑ד כָּל־הַ֝יּ֗וֹם קֹדֵ֥ר הִלָּֽכְתִּי׃

records.literal_gloss: I am bent, I am bowed down exceedingly; all the day mourning I go about.

en.L: I am bent down, I am bowed over exceedingly; all day long I go about mourning.
en.B: I am bent over, bowed down completely; I spend the whole day going about in grief.
en.R: I am bent over and bowed down low. I am sad and grieving all day long.

decisions.choice: mourning: dark, in the dress of grief
decisions.reason: The word (qoder) means dark or dirty: a mourner went about unwashed and in dark clothes (Psalm 35:14).

source.text: כִּֽי־כְ֭סָלַי מָלְא֣וּ נִקְלֶ֑ה וְאֵ֥ין מְ֝תֹ֗ם בִּבְשָׂרִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: For my loins are filled with burning, and there is no soundness in my flesh.

en.L: For my loins are full of burning, and there is no soundness in my flesh.
en.B: A burning fever fills my sides, and nothing in my body is well.
en.R: My body burns with fever and pain. Nothing in me is healthy.

decisions.choice: loins: the muscles of the back and sides
decisions.reason: The word (kesalim) is the inner muscles of the lower back, near the kidneys.

decisions.choice: burning: inflammation, fever
decisions.reason: The word (niqleh) most likely comes from a verb meaning to roast or scorch; a verb with the same letters means to be despised, so some read "my insides are full of disgrace".

decisions.choice: no soundness in my flesh: as in verse 4
decisions.reason: The line repeats verse 4, closing the description of his body.

source.text: נְפוּג֣וֹתִי וְנִדְכֵּ֣יתִי עַד־מְאֹ֑ד שָׁ֝אַ֗גְתִּי מִֽנַּהֲמַ֥ת לִבִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: I am numb and crushed exceedingly; I roar from the groaning of my heart.

en.L: I am numb and crushed exceedingly; I roar from the groaning of my heart.
en.B: I have gone numb and am crushed to the core; my heart groans, and I cry out aloud.
en.R: I am weak and completely broken. My heart hurts so much that I cry out loud.

decisions.choice: roar: cry out loudly
decisions.reason: The verb (sha'ag) is used of a lion's roar; here it is a loud cry of pain (Psalm 22:2).

decisions.choice: numb: faint, gone cold
decisions.reason: The verb (pug) is to grow numb or faint, as Jacob's heart did at news too great to take in (Genesis 45:26).

source.text: אֲֽדֹנָי נֶגְדְּךָ֥ כָל־תַּאֲוָתִ֑י וְ֝אַנְחָתִ֗י מִמְּךָ֥ לֹא־נִסְתָּֽרָה׃

records.literal_gloss: Lord, before you [is] all my longing, and my sighing from you is not hidden.

en.L: Lord, before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [is] all my longing, and my sighing is not hidden from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.B: Lord, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} see everything I long for; not one of my sighs escapes {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.R: Lord, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know everything I want so badly. You hear every one of my sighs.

decisions.choice: Lord: the title 'Adonai
decisions.reason: Here the psalmist uses the title 'Adonai, "my Lord", not the divine name; it comes again in verses 16 and 23.

decisions.choice: longing: what he longs for, healing and help
decisions.reason: The word (ta'avah) is desire; here it is all the psalmist longs for, set before God as a prayer.

source.text: לִבִּ֣י סְ֭חַרְחַר עֲזָבַ֣נִי כֹחִ֑י וְֽאוֹר־עֵינַ֥י גַּם־הֵ֝֗ם אֵ֣ין אִתִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: My heart throbs; my strength has left me, and the light of my eyes, also they are not with me.

en.L: My heart throbs; my strength has left me, and the light of my eyes, even that is not with me.
en.B: My heart races; my strength has deserted me; the light of my eyes, that too is gone.
en.R: My heart is racing. I have no strength left. My eyes have grown dim.

decisions.choice: throbs: beats fast
decisions.reason: The verb (secharchar) is rare: a doubled form of a verb meaning to go around, used of a heart that pounds.

decisions.choice: the light of my eyes: life and clear sight
decisions.reason: Bright eyes are a sign of health and life (Proverbs 15:30); dim eyes, of weakness.

source.text: אֹֽהֲבַ֨י׀וְרֵעַ֗י מִנֶּ֣גֶד נִגְעִ֣י יַעֲמֹ֑דוּ וּ֝קְרוֹבַ֗י מֵרָחֹ֥ק עָמָֽדוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: My friends and my companions stand aloof from my plague, and my near ones stand far off.

en.L: My friends and my companions stand back from my affliction, and my near ones stand far off.
en.B: My friends and companions keep away from my sickness; even my own family stands at a distance.
en.R: My friends and neighbors stay away because I am sick. Even my family keeps away from me.

decisions.choice: affliction: a blow, a plague
decisions.reason: The word (nega') is a stroke or blow, often a skin disease (Leviticus 13:2); it can imply a blow from God.

decisions.choice: my near ones stand far off: a play on words
decisions.reason: Those who should be "near" (qerovim, relatives) stand "far" away.

source.text: וַיְנַקְשׁ֤וּ׀מְבַקְשֵׁ֬י נַפְשִׁ֗י וְדֹרְשֵׁ֣י רָ֭עָתִי דִּבְּר֣וּ הַוּ֑וֹת וּ֝מִרְמ֗וֹת כָּל־הַיּ֥וֹם יֶהְגּֽוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they lay snares, those who seek my life, and those who seek my harm speak ruin, and deceits all the day they murmur.

en.L: Those who seek my life lay snares, and those who seek my harm speak of ruin and murmur deceits all day long.
en.B: Those who want my life set traps; those who want to hurt me speak of destroying me and mutter lies all day long.
en.R: People who want to kill me set traps for me. People who want to hurt me talk about how to ruin me. All day long they make up lies.

decisions.choice: lay snares: set traps, as a hunter of birds
decisions.reason: The verb (naqash) is to set a trap (Psalm 9:17).

decisions.choice: murmur: plot under the breath
decisions.reason: The verb (hagah) is the one used for murmuring God's instruction in 1:2 and for the wise words of 37:30; here the enemies murmur lies.

source.text: וַאֲנִ֣י כְ֭חֵרֵשׁ לֹ֣א אֶשְׁמָ֑ע וּ֝כְאִלֵּ֗ם לֹ֣א יִפְתַּח־פִּֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And I [am] like a deaf [one], I do not hear, and like a mute [one who] does not open his mouth.

en.L: But I [am] like a deaf [person]; I do not hear; and like a mute [person who] does not open {{gender:their|his}} mouth.
en.B: But I act as if I were deaf and hear nothing, as if I were mute and could not open my mouth.
en.R: But I act like a deaf person who does not hear them. I am like someone who cannot speak. I say nothing at all.

decisions.choice: deaf and mute: no answer to the enemies
decisions.reason: The psalmist does not answer his accusers but leaves his case with the LORD (verse 16); compare the servant who did not open his mouth (Isaiah 53:7).

decisions.choice: inclusive wording by default; the traditional "he" or "man" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses a masculine singular for a person who stands for anyone of this kind, so the gender setting gives inclusive wording by default and the traditional form as the alternative.

decisions.choice: as if I were deaf ... mute
alternatives: like the deaf ... like the mute
decisions.reason: Balanced says plainly that the psalmist is choosing silence, which the simile means.

source.text: וָאֱהִ֗י כְּ֭אִישׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־שֹׁמֵ֑עַ וְאֵ֥ין בְּ֝פִ֗יו תּוֹכָחֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And I have become like a man who does not hear and in whose mouth [are] no arguments.

en.L: I have become like {{gender:someone|a man}} who does not hear, and in whose mouth [are] no replies.
en.B: I have turned into someone who hears nothing and has no answer to give.
en.R: I am like someone who cannot hear and has nothing to say back.

decisions.choice: arguments: a reply in one's defense
decisions.reason: The word (tokhachot) is an argument or rebuke, the kind of reply one makes in a dispute or a court (Job 23:4).

decisions.choice: inclusive wording by default; the traditional "he" or "man" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses a masculine singular for a person who stands for anyone of this kind, so the gender setting gives inclusive wording by default and the traditional form as the alternative.

source.text: כִּֽי־לְךָ֣ יְהוָ֣ה הוֹחָ֑לְתִּי אַתָּ֥ה תַ֝עֲנֶ֗ה אֲדֹנָ֥י אֱלֹהָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: For for you, YHWH, I have waited; you will answer, Lord my God.

en.L: For for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I have waited; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will answer, Lord my God.
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, my hope is fixed on {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the one who will answer, Lord my God.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I am trusting in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Lord my God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will answer me.

decisions.choice: you will answer: the stressed "you"
decisions.reason: The pronoun is stressed: the psalmist gives no answer to his enemies (verses 14-15), because the LORD himself will answer.

decisions.choice: waited: waited in hope
decisions.reason: The verb (yachal) is to wait with hope (Psalm 31:25).

source.text: כִּֽי־אָ֭מַרְתִּי פֶּן־יִשְׂמְחוּ־לִ֑י בְּמ֥וֹט רַ֝גְלִ֗י עָלַ֥י הִגְדִּֽילוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For I said, Lest they rejoice over me; when my foot slips, against me they magnify themselves.

en.L: For I said, "Lest they rejoice over me, [those who], when my foot slips, magnify themselves against me."
en.B: For I said, "Do not let them enjoy my fall; when my foot slips, they lord it over me."
en.R: I said, "Do not let my enemies be happy about my troubles. When I slip, they act as if they are better than me."

decisions.choice: lest: a fear turned into a prayer
decisions.reason: The word (pen, "lest") states what the psalmist fears; said to God, it becomes a request that it not happen.

decisions.choice: my foot slips: I fall into trouble
decisions.reason: A slipping foot is a picture of falling into disaster (Psalm 94:18).

decisions.choice: my enemies
decisions.reason: Readable names who "they" are, from verses 13 and 20.

source.text: כִּֽי־אֲ֭נִי לְצֶ֣לַע נָכ֑וֹן וּמַכְאוֹבִ֖י נֶגְדִּ֣י תָמִֽיד׃

records.literal_gloss: For I [am] ready for stumbling, and my pain [is] before me continually.

en.L: For I [am] ready to stumble, and my pain [is] before me continually.
en.B: I am on the edge of collapse, and my pain never leaves my sight.
en.R: I could fall at any moment. My pain is with me all the time.

decisions.choice: stumbling: falling, limping
decisions.reason: The word (tsela') is a stumble or a limp (Psalm 35:15).

decisions.choice: before me continually: always in view
decisions.reason: His pain is always before his eyes; he cannot forget it.

source.text: כִּֽי־עֲוֺנִ֥י אַגִּ֑יד אֶ֝דְאַ֗ג מֵֽחַטָּאתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: For my iniquity I declare; I am anxious because of my sin.

en.L: For I declare my iniquity; I am anxious because of my sin.
en.B: I openly admit my guilt; my sin weighs on me with dread.
en.R: I admit the wrong things I have done. I am deeply troubled by my sin.

decisions.choice: declare: confess
decisions.reason: The verb (higgid) is to tell or make known; here, to confess openly (compare 32:5).

decisions.choice: anxious: troubled, full of dread
decisions.reason: The verb (da'ag) is to worry or be anxious; his sin weighs on him.

source.text: וְֽ֭אֹיְבַי חַיִּ֣ים עָצֵ֑מוּ וְרַבּ֖וּ שֹׂנְאַ֣י שָֽׁקֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: And my enemies [are] living, they are strong, and many are those who hate me falsely.

en.L: But my enemies [are] alive [and] strong, and many [are] those who hate me falsely.
en.B: Meanwhile my enemies are full of life and strength; many hate me for no good reason.
en.R: But my enemies are healthy and strong. Many people hate me for no reason.

decisions.choice: living: alive and well
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads chayyim, "living", that is, healthy and vigorous, in contrast to the sick psalmist. Some propose chinnam, "without cause", which differs by one letter and would match "falsely" in the next line, as in 35:19. The renderings follow the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: falsely: wrongly, without cause
decisions.reason: The word (sheqer, a lie) here describes hatred with no true reason behind it.

source.text: וּמְשַׁלְּמֵ֣י רָ֭עָה תַּ֣חַת טוֹבָ֑ה יִ֝שְׂטְנ֗וּנִי תַּ֣חַת רָֽדְפִי־טֽוֹב׃

records.literal_gloss: And those who repay evil instead of good accuse me, because I pursue good.

en.L: And those who repay evil in place of good accuse me, because I pursue [what is] good.
en.B: Those who return evil for kindness act as my accusers, because I go after what is good.
en.R: I have been good to them, but they do evil to me in return. They accuse me because I try to do what is right.

decisions.choice: accuse: act as an adversary
decisions.reason: The verb (satan) is to oppose or accuse; the related noun is used of an accuser in a court (Psalm 109:6) and of the Accuser in Job 1.

decisions.choice: evil for good: enemies who repay kindness with harm
decisions.reason: The psalmist has done them good; his confession of sin (verse 19) is to God, not an admission that his enemies are right (35:12).

decisions.choice: I have been good to them
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the exchange in two plain sentences.

source.text: אַל־תַּֽעַזְבֵ֥נִי יְהוָ֑ה אֱ֝לֹהַ֗י אַל־תִּרְחַ֥ק מִמֶּֽנִּי׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not forsake me, YHWH; my God, do not be far from me.

en.L: Do not forsake me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}; my God, do not be far from me.
en.B: Do not abandon me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}; my God, do not stay far from me.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, do not leave me alone. My God, stay close to me.

decisions.choice: do not be far from me: a cry heard in other psalms
decisions.reason: The same plea comes in Psalm 22:12, 20 and 35:22; the friends who "stand far off" (verse 12) make God's nearness the more urgent.

source.text: ח֥וּשָׁה לְעֶזְרָתִ֑י אֲ֝דֹנָ֗י תְּשׁוּעָתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Make haste to my help, Lord, my salvation.

en.L: Make haste to my help, Lord, my salvation.
en.B: Be quick to help me, Lord, my salvation.
en.R: Lord, hurry and help me! You are the one who saves me.

decisions.choice: my salvation: the one who rescues me
decisions.reason: The word (teshu'ah) is rescue (37:39); calling the Lord "my salvation" names him as the one who saves.

decisions.choice: the psalm ends with a plea
decisions.reason: The psalm closes still asking; it gives no word that the answer has come, only trust that it will (verse 16).
